newsitem.title: POLAND: Gdansk Shipyard administrator sees October tender.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk Shipyard administrator sees October tender.

text.p: The administrator of Poland's bankrupt Gdansk Shipyard will announce a tender for the yard in October, the daily Rzeczpospolita reported on Saturday.
"In October a tender will be announced for the sale of the bankrupt Stocznia Gdanska SA," the paper quoted Michal Lachert as saying.

Lachert told Reuters earlier in the week he had received offers by two foreign consortia to invest in the shipyard, one from a Polish company with Norwegian capital, ready to invest $200 million, and the other from a Vienna-based company.
He did not give any details about the second offer. @
Lachert told Rzeczpospolita that for the tender to be called next month an appraisal of the firm's assets had to be conducted.
The Gdansk Shipyard, where Lech Walesa's Solidarity union was born 16 years ago, has debts of 414 million zlotys ($151 million) while its assets are worth about 350 million zlotys.
The shareholders of the shipyard, in which the treasury has a majority, decided to file for bankruptcy in June after the yard's debts exceeded its assets and banks denied it loans. @

Lachert told Rzeczpospolita that it would take three to six months to prepare the yard for its sale and that an injection of funds from the government or a goverment guarantee on loans might be necessary.
"I can't imagine that without a guarantee some bank or bank consortium would decide to finance the shipyard," he said.
